title: Oracle Certified Professional (OCP) – Java SE 11 Developer
overview: The Oracle Certified Professional (OCP) – Java SE 11 Developer course is designed to provide in-depth knowledge of Java SE 11 features and best practices. This course prepares participants for the OCP certification exam by covering core Java SE 11 programming concepts, advanced features, and development techniques.
audience: Java developers looking to advance their skills and certification.
IT professionals preparing for the OCP Java SE 11 certification exam.
Software engineers and programmers who want to deepen their Java knowledge.
Individuals interested in learning advanced Java programming techniques and best practices.
methodology: Lectures and Presentations: Comprehensive explanations of Java SE 11 features and programming concepts.
Hands-On Labs: Practical exercises for coding, debugging, and optimizing Java applications.
Case Studies: Real-world scenarios to apply Java SE 11 concepts and techniques.
Group Discussions: Interactive sessions to explore Java development challenges and solutions.
Quizzes and Practice Exams: Assessments to gauge understanding and readiness for the certification exam.
competencies: Advanced Java SE 11 features and APIs
objectivesIntro: By the end of the course, participants will be able to:
objectives: To provide a thorough understanding of Java SE 11 features and programming techniques.
To prepare participants for the Oracle Certified Professional (OCP) – Java SE 11 Developer exam.
To equip learners with practical skills for developing, debugging, and optimizing Java applications.
To familiarize participants with best practices and advanced Java programming concepts.

items.text: Overview of Java SE 11 and New Features
Understanding Java Language Basics and Syntax
Working with Java Data Types, Operators, and Control Statements
Introduction to Java Modules and Project Jigsaw
Exploring New APIs (e.g., HTTP Client API, Collection API Enhancements)
Designing and Implementing Classes and Objects
Working with Interfaces and Abstract Classes
Understanding Java I/O Streams (File I/O, Object I/O)
Working with Java NIO (Buffers, Channels, Files)
Using Path, File, and Directory Operations
Using Generics and Type Safety in Collections
Overview of JDBC and Database Operations
Connecting to Databases and Executing SQL Queries
Using Data Source and Connection Pooling
Best Practices for Secure Coding and Application Development
